mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה holds a captive woman keeps her sanctity, the three-month wait argued by רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, and why two פסוקים teach that one act brings only one punishment.
overview: Earlier on the daf, רבי יהודה ruled that a captive woman stays in her sanctity, meaning we do not assume she was violated. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא where he makes a גיורת wait three months before marrying. רב יוסף answers that a convert does not guard herself, but a captive does. Then a ברייתא is brought where רבי יהודה makes a שבויה herself wait, and רב יוסף has no answer. רב ששת's answer is reported: that ברייתא is about a captive seen being violated. רבה first explains that רבי יוסי lets her marry right away because she used a מוך. That fails for a maidservant freed suddenly through שן ועין and for a raped or seduced woman. So רבה says instead that such a woman turns over afterward, while רבי יהודה worries she did not do it properly. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's פסוק 'ולא יהיה אסון' and explains why both it and 'כדי רשעתו' are needed. It begins asking how this works for רבי מאיר, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the convert who must wait three months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really says a captive keeps her sanctity, quoting a ברייתא where he makes a convert wait three months before marrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that a captive stays in her sanctity? But a ברייתא teaches: a woman who converted and saw blood — רבי יהודה says her impurity starts only from the moment she saw it. רבי יוסי says she is like all women and makes things impure going back 24 hours, or back to her last check. And she must wait three months before marrying, says רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי lets her get engaged and married right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה's earlier ruling about a captive by quoting a ברייתא where he seems worried that a woman had relations before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה makes a גיורת wait three months because he worries she might be pregnant from before her conversion. That shows he assumes she had relations. So why would he assume a captive did not have relations and stays in her sanctity?

keyTerms.meaning: She stays in her sanctity, meaning we do not assume she was violated
Her time is enough: her impurity starts only from when she saw the blood
To wait three months, so we know whether she is pregnant

steps.confusionAlert: The first half of the ברייתא, about seeing blood, is not what the challenge is about. It is quoted only because it is part of the same ברייתא. The challenge comes from the second half, about waiting three months.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda really hold that she remains in her sanctity?
phrases.notes: "She" is the captive woman from רבי יהודה's ruling earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
A convert who converted and saw blood,
Rabbi Yehuda says: her time is enough for her.
phrases.notes: He means she is impure only from the moment she saw the blood, not earlier.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּכׇל הַנָּשִׁים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: she is like all women,
and she makes things impure for the past twenty-four hours,
or from examination to examination.
phrases.notes: Meaning back to the last time she checked herself and found she was clean.

phrases.english: And she must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits her to be betrothed and to marry immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּקְדוּשְׁתַּהּ קָיְימָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's ruling about a captive from earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that a captive remains in her sanctity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה worries that a גיורת had relations and might be pregnant, he should worry the same about a captive.

steps.title: A convert does not guard herself, a captive does
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the two cases are different: a convert had no reason to stay away from relations, but a captive works hard to protect herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you comparing a convert to a captive? A convert does not guard herself, but a captive does guard herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects the comparison. He says a convert and a captive are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before converting, a woman lived freely and had no reason to avoid relations, so רבי יהודה worries about her. A Jewish captive cares about her sanctity and fights to protect herself, so we may assume she was not violated.

keyTerms.meaning: You are setting one case against another, raising a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גִּיּוֹרֶת אַשְּׁבוּיָהּ קָא רָמֵית?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you raising a contradiction from a convert to a captive?
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering רב פפא בר שמואל, who raised the question earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: A convert does not guard herself,
a captive guards herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A convert and a captive are the same, so רבי יהודה contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: A convert does not guard herself and a captive does, so the rulings fit together.

steps.title: Challenge from a captive who must wait three months
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה makes a captive herself wait three months, and רב יוסף has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then contrasted a captive with a captive, as a ברייתא teaches: A convert, a captive, and a maidservant who converted, were redeemed, or were freed when older than three years and one day must wait three months, says רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי lets them get engaged and married right away. רב יוסף was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The question comes back stronger: now there is a ברייתא where רבי יהודה worries about a captive herself, and רב יוסף cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer of step 2 worked only because the first case was a convert. Here the very same kind of woman, a שבויה, must wait three months, so רבי יהודה seems to worry she had relations. That directly contradicts his ruling that a captive stays in her sanctity.

keyTerms.meaning: Who were redeemed, bought back from captivity
He was silent; he had no answer

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a convert and a captive no longer helps, so the גמרא needs a new way to explain רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction from a captive to a captive, as it is taught in a baraita:
The convert, the captive, and the maidservant
who were redeemed, converted, or freed

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵירוֹת עַל בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: when older than three years and one day —
must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits them to be betrothed and to marry immediately.
He was silent.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף had no answer at that moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the answer of step 2 by bringing a ברייתא about a captive herself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that a captive remains in her sanctity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא רבי יהודה makes a captive wait three months, so he must worry she had relations, which contradicts his other ruling about the same kind of woman.

steps.title: Have you heard an answer to this?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב פפא בר שמואל whether he has heard any answer to his own question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף has no answer, he asks the questioner whether he knows one. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is decided yet. The question opens the door for an answer from an earlier teacher, רב ששת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After being silent, רב יוסף asks for a known answer to the challenge of step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a known answer to the contradiction about a captive.

steps.title: The case is a captive who was seen being violated
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל quotes רב ששת: the ברייתא that requires waiting speaks about a captive whom people saw being violated.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said: it is talking about a case where they saw that she was violated.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the second ברייתא is a special case where witnesses saw the captive being violated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule that a captive stays in her sanctity means we do not assume she was violated when no one knows. But if she was seen being violated, the presumption is gone, and now there is a real worry she is pregnant, so she must wait three months. The two rulings no longer contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said (quoting a teacher)
That they saw her being violated

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: an unknown captive stays in her sanctity, but a captive seen being violated must wait three months because she may be pregnant.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
It is where they saw that she had relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, שֶׁרָאוּהָ שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and settles the contradiction of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא requiring three months is about a captive known to have been violated, not an ordinary captive.

steps.title: Then why does רבי יוסי allow her to marry right away?
steps.stepSummary: If she was seen being violated, the גמרא asks how רבי יוסי can let her marry immediately without worrying that she is pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer creates a new problem, this time for רבי יוסי, who lets her marry immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the case is a woman who certainly had relations. So there is a real chance she is pregnant, and רבי יוסי should also require her to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי?
phrases.english: If so, what is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 5 to question the other side of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that she may marry immediately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she was surely violated, there is a real worry she is pregnant, so how can she marry without waiting?

steps.title: רבי יוסי assumes she used a contraceptive
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי יוסי holds that a woman having forbidden relations uses a מוך so she will not become pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי יוסי holds that a woman who has forbidden relations uses a contraceptive pad so that she will not become pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives רבי יוסי's reason: he assumes the woman protected herself from pregnancy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי agrees the woman had relations, but he assumes she used a מוך to block pregnancy. So there is no real worry she is pregnant, and no need to wait three months.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has forbidden relations
A soft pad placed in the body to prevent pregnancy
So that she will not become pregnant

phrases.english: Rabba said: Rabbi Yosei holds:
a woman who has forbidden relations uses a contraceptive pad,
so that she will not become pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by explaining רבי יוסי's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning behind the opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman who surely had relations might be pregnant, so even רבי יוסי should require waiting.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי assumes she used a מוך, so there is no worry about pregnancy and she may marry immediately.

steps.title: The contraceptive answer fails for a maidservant freed through tooth or eye
steps.stepSummary: A גיורת, a שבויה and a שפחה all know in advance that their status may change, so they would use a מוך. A שפחה freed through שן ועין gets no warning, so the מוך answer does not work for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, a convert plans to convert, so she protects herself. A captive does not know where she is being taken, so she protects herself too. A maidservant heard from her master that he will free her, so she also protects herself. But a maidservant freed because her master knocked out her tooth or eye had no warning. What can we say about her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's answer from step 7, that רבי יוסי assumes the woman used a מוך. It shows one case where she had no reason to plan ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוך is used before relations, so it only makes sense if the woman expected her status to change. The convert, the captive and the maidservant who was told she will be freed all had a reason to protect themselves. A maidservant freed suddenly through שן ועין did not, yet רבי יוסי still lets her marry right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (it introduces a contrast with a case that does not)
A non-Jewish maidservant who is being freed
A maidservant who goes free because her master knocked out her tooth or eye (שמות 21:26-27)

phrases.english: Granted, a convert;
since she intends to convert,
she guards herself.
phrases.notes: He means she protects herself from getting pregnant by using a מוך, as רבה said in step 7.

phrases.english: A captive too,
since she does not know where they are taking her.
A maidservant too, since she heard it from her master's mouth.
phrases.notes: She heard her master say he plans to free her, so she had time to prepare.

phrases.english: But one who goes free through tooth or eye,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יוֹצְאָה בְּשֵׁן וָעַיִן, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's מוך explanation from step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי יוסי relies on the woman using a מוך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מוך requires planning ahead, but a maidservant freed suddenly through שן ועין had no warning, yet רבי יוסי still permits her right away.

steps.title: Blocking a possible defense with the case of a raped or seduced woman
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that רבי יוסי does not rule leniently in sudden cases. The גמרא rejects this from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי lets a raped or seduced woman marry right away, even though that also happens without warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי יוסי did not give his lenient ruling for anything that happens on its own, look at a raped or seduced woman, which happens on its own. It was taught: a raped or seduced woman must wait three months, says רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי allows her to become engaged and to marry right away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save the מוך answer and then knocks it down, which makes the question from step 8 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested defense is that רבי יוסי agrees with רבי יהודה in surprise cases. But rape and seduction are surprise cases too, and רבי יוסי is still lenient there. So something other than a מוך must explain his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)
On its own, without any planning
To wait three months, so it is clear whether she is pregnant

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a new question. It closes off an escape route so the question from step 8 still stands.

phrases.english: And if you will say

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִמֵּילָא לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: that for anything that happens on its own, Rabbi Yosei did not say his ruling,
look at a raped or seduced woman, which happens on its own,
and it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנוּסָה וּמְפוּתָּה צְרִיכוֹת לְהַמְתִּין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: A raped woman and a seduced woman must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits them to become engaged and to marry right away!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כֹּל מִמֵּילָא לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible defense against the question in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested limit that רבי יוסי is only lenient in cases that were planned
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי is lenient even for a raped or seduced woman, which happens without warning

steps.title: רבה's new reason: the woman turns over to avoid pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: רבה changes his explanation. רבי יוסי holds that a woman in forbidden relations turns over afterward so she will not become pregnant, which works even when nothing was planned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: רבי יוסי holds that a woman having forbidden relations turns over so that she will not become pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the מוך answer failed, רבה gives a new reason for רבי יוסי that also covers surprise cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוך is used before relations, but turning over happens afterward. So even a woman who was surprised, like the maidservant freed through שן ועין or the raped woman, can still prevent pregnancy. This explains all of רבי יוסי's lenient rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
Turns over (after relations, to prevent pregnancy)

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
Rabbi Yosei holds:
a woman having forbidden relations turns over
so that she will not become pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 8-9 by replacing the מוך explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reason with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי relies on a מוך used before relations, which needs planning
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי relies on the woman turning over afterward, which works even without planning
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the final explanation of the argument between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה about waiting three months.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה say to this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה answers this reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה still requires waiting if women turn over to avoid pregnancy. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there is a good reason to be lenient, the גמרא needs to know why the other תנא disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (How does the other opinion answer this?)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה, who requires her to wait three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יהודה responds to רבה's reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה does not accept the turning-over reason

steps.title: רבי יהודה worries she did not turn over properly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is concerned that she may not have turned over well enough, so she might be pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that maybe she did not turn over properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה agrees women turn over, but he does not trust that it always works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two do not argue about what women do. They argue about whether we may rely on it. רבי יהודה is stricter and makes her wait three months.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: she turns over afterward to avoid pregnancy, so she may marry right away. רבי יהודה: she might not have done it properly, so she waits three months.

phrases.english: We are concerned
that perhaps she did not turn over properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא לֹא נֶהֶפְכָה יָפֶה יָפֶה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה fears the turning over was not done well enough, so pregnancy is still possible

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's verse: 'and yet no harm follow'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which proves from 'ולא יהיה אסון ענוש יענש' that one who is liable to death does not also pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And yet no harm follow, he shall surely be punished,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of someone who strikes a pregnant woman. Only when there is no death ('אסון') does he pay, which shows that one who is liable to death does not pay money as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be punished (with a money payment)

phrases.english: As it says: "And yet no harm follow,"
"he shall surely be punished," etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְלֹא יִהְיֶה אָסוֹן עָנוֹשׁ יֵעָנֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the three-month discussion to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'ולא יהיה אסון' the משנה learns that one who is liable to death is exempt from paying

steps.title: Isn't this already learned from 'according to his wickedness'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs this פסוק, since 'כדי רשעתו' already teaches that a person is punished for one wrong and not for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really learned from here? It is learned from there: 'according to his wickedness.' You punish him for one wickedness, but you do not punish him for two wickednesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's choice of source by pointing to a different פסוק that already teaches the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כדי רשעתו' (דברים 25:2) teaches that one act brings only one punishment. That alone would mean someone liable to death does not also pay. So why does the משנה use 'ולא יהיה אסון'?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really learned from here?
It is learned from there (another source)
A wrongdoing, meaning a punishment for one wrong

phrases.english: Is it really learned from here?
It is learned from there:
"according to his wickedness,"
you punish him for one wickedness,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת!
phrases.english: but you do not punish him for two wickednesses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source quoted in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's use of 'ולא יהיה אסון' as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'כדי רשעתו' already teaches that one act brings only one punishment, so the משנה's פסוק seems unnecessary

steps.title: Each verse teaches a different pair of punishments
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק teaches the rule for death plus money. The other teaches it for lashes plus money.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse is about death and money, and the other verse is about lashes and money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 14 by giving each פסוק its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked why the משנה needs 'ולא יהיה אסון' when 'כדי רשעתו' already teaches 'one punishment, not two.' The answer is that the two פסוקים cover different cases. 'ולא יהיה אסון' covers death plus money, and 'כדי רשעתו' covers lashes plus money.

phrases.english: One is about death and money,
phrases.notes: This is 'ולא יהיה אסון' (שמות 21:22), the פסוק the משנה used.

phrases.english: and one is about lashes and money.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא בְּמִיתָה וּמָמוֹן, וַחֲדָא בְּמַלְקוֹת וּמָמוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק covers a different pair of punishments.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים seemed to teach the same thing, so one looked extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ולא יהיה אסון' covers death plus money, and 'כדי רשעתו' covers lashes plus money.

steps.title: Why both cases had to be written
steps.stepSummary: Each case has its own reason for exempting, so neither could be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the תורה taught only death and money, I would say the exemption is because a life is lost, and with lashes and money no life is lost, so I would say no. If it taught only lashes and money, I would say the exemption is because the sin is not severe, but with death and money the sin is severe, so I would say no. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a צריכא. It shows that we could not learn the death case from the lashes case, or the lashes case from the death case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With death, you might think he skips paying only because losing his life is the biggest punishment there is. Lashes do not take a life, so that reason would not carry over. With lashes, you might think he is let off because the sin is lighter, but a death-penalty sin is much more severe. Since each case has a reason that might not apply to the other, the תורה had to write both.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary (both teachings are needed)
I might say no (the rule does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'one punishment, not two' applies both to death plus money and to lashes plus money. Each one needs its own פסוק, because each has its own possible reason.
steps.confusionAlert: The two reasons point in opposite directions. Death is a heavier punishment, but the lashes case involves a lighter sin. That is exactly why neither case can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And both are necessary:
for if it had taught us only death and money,
that is because there is loss of life,
but lashes and money,
where there is no loss of life, I would say no.
And if it had taught us only lashes and money,
that is because its prohibition is not severe.
But death and money,
where its prohibition is severe, I would say no.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the answer of step 15 by showing that neither case can be learned from the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has its own reason that might not carry over to the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe one פסוק would have been enough to cover both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has a different reason it might be exempt, so both פסוקים are needed.

steps.title: According to רבי מאיר, why are two verses needed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that someone liable for lashes and money gets both. So what is the second פסוק for?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, who says a person is flogged and also pays, why do I need two verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 15 from the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 15 used 'כדי רשעתו' for lashes plus money. But רבי מאיר holds that a person gets lashes and also pays, so for him that פסוק cannot be teaching an exemption in the lashes case. That leaves both פסוקים looking like they teach the death case, so one seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: he is flogged and also pays

phrases.english: And according to רבי מאיר, who said
one is flogged and also pays,
why do I need two verses?
phrases.notes: He means the two פסוקים from before: 'ולא יהיה אסון' and 'כדי רשעתו'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם, תַּרְתֵּי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15 using the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The split in step 15 that gives 'כדי רשעתו' to lashes plus money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי מאיר, lashes and money are both given, so 'כדי רשעתו' cannot teach an exemption there. Both פסוקים then seem to teach the same death case.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר, one verse is still about death and money
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts: one פסוק teaches the death plus money case. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse is about death and money,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question about רבי מאיר. Only the first half of the answer appears here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for רבי מאיר, one פסוק still teaches that someone liable for death does not also pay. What the second פסוק teaches according to him is explained on the next amud.

phrases.english: One verse is about death and money,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases again, in a way that fits רבי מאיר (completed in the following lines).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי מאיר, the second פסוק seems to have no job.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק covers death plus money. The second פסוק's job is given in the next lines.
